stem: A histogram is drawn for classes of unequal width: 0-10, 10-30, 30-40, 40-70, 70-80. Because the widths differ, the y-axis plots frequency DENSITY (frequency per unit width), and the bar heights read 2, 3, 5, 1, 4 respectively. What is the total number of observations represented?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Reads the bar heights 2, 3, 5, 1, 4 directly as the class frequencies and sums them to 15, assuming equal-width bars. With unequal widths the height is a density, so each must be multiplied by its width.
Assumes every class has the same width 10 and multiplies each density by 10: (2+3+5+1+4)*10 = 150. The classes 10-30 and 40-70 are wider, so a uniform width understates the total.
Misreads the width of class 40-70 as 50 instead of 30: 2*10 + 3*20 + 5*10 + 1*50 + 4*10 = 220. The width of 40-70 is 30.

explanation: On an unequal-width histogram the bar height is frequency density (frequency per unit width), so frequency = density * width, computed class by class. Widths are 10, 20, 10, 30, 10; frequencies are 20, 60, 50, 30, 40; total = 200. Reading the heights as frequencies (equal-width assumption) gives only 15, and applying a uniform width of 10 gives 150.

explanation_sections.punchline: On an unequal-width histogram the height is density, so frequency = density * width per class: 2*10 + 3*20 + 5*10 + 1*30 + 4*10 = 200, not the bare sum of heights.
explanation_sections.approach: Model: frequency recovery from a density histogram with unequal class widths. Assumption: bar area, not height, equals frequency, so each frequency = height * width. Recipe in four steps. (1) Compute each width: 10, 20, 10, 30, 10. (2) Multiply each density by its width: 20, 60, 50, 30, 40. (3) These are the class frequencies. (4) Total = 20 + 60 + 50 + 30 + 40 = 200.
explanation_sections.lesson: When class widths are unequal, a histogram plots frequency density; recover each frequency as density times width (area of the bar), never read the height as the frequency.
explanation_sections.timing: About 145 seconds: five width-times-height products and one sum. Reject 15 instantly: it is the sum of the heights, which only works when every class width is equal.
